Multi-vendor review (codex gpt-5.5, grok grok-4.5, pi qwen3-coder; antigravity failed with invalid JSON - quorum 3/4) over the full branch c6d8eefb..5883748a. 49 raw findings, all re-verified here by direct execution. None re-opens a round-7 defect; the implementation itself is sound. Full detail in reviews/round-8/synthesis.md.

blocking_findings: B1 BLOCKING (codex-001, grok-001, reproduced): `make test` - a target this change introduces in packages/gen-eval/Makefile - exits 1 on a clean tree. `uv run pytest -q -m "not slow"` does not exclude the integration marker, so it collects 7 tests that resolve scenarios to <repo>/evaluation/gen_eval/scenarios/<category>, a coordinator-repo path absent from this tree (tests/test_integration_scenarios.py:45, tests/test_integration_orchestrator.py:34). CI is green only because the workflow uses -m "not e2e and not integration". The failures predate the change; the permanently-red target that surfaces them does not.

B2 BLOCKING (codex-002, grok-002, reproduced): specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md:213-227 requires reclamation to `SHALL increment the descriptor contract version`, with a matching scenario. Observed CONTRACT_VERSION == "2", VERSION == 2, all three schemas at x-gen-eval-contract-version 2, and an empty diff of contracts/__init__.py against the merge base. The refusal is deliberate and correct per round-7 finding 9 and DOWNSTREAM.md:192-197; the spec was never amended. handoffs/plan-2.json decision 3 is the superseded source. Blocking because the delta spec archives into openspec/specs/ and would publish a durable requirement this change's own implementation violates. descriptor.py:413 repeats the stale claim.

decisions.title: Verdict not_converged on two blocking findings with two-vendor convergence
decisions.rationale: Both were reproduced here by direct execution, not accepted on vendor assertion. Neither re-opens a round-7 defect, and both fixes are narrow - a Makefile selector and a spec paragraph plus a docstring.

decisions.title: B2 is blocking, not a nit, and the fix is to the spec rather than the code
decisions.rationale: Two vendors rated it nit. The delta spec is what archives into openspec/specs/, so merging as-is publishes a durable requirement the implementation violates and the next author either bumps CONTRACT_VERSION for no reason or concludes the code is wrong. Round-7 finding 9 established that reclaiming a Python export name is not a breaking JSON Schema change, so the code is right and the requirement is stale.

decisions.title: B1 is attributed to this change even though the failing tests predate it
decisions.rationale: packages/gen-eval/Makefile is new here. A default developer test target that can never pass gets ignored as fast as one that can never fail, and the next real failure inside it will be invisible.

decisions.title: H1 raised on my own verification rather than vendor report
decisions.rationale: Three of the five flag-surface.yaml scenarios assert an observable that the CLI emits identically when the flag under test is omitted (verified by running the fixture without --mode, --report-format json and --no-services). The file's own header forbids exactly this. Three of the ten units the D11 gate counts as exercised rest on it. Root cause is expressive: ExpectBlock has error_contains but no negative string or file-absence assertion, so the intended check is inexpressible.

decisions.title: Pi's findings discounted; antigravity's failure is a known dispatcher defect
decisions.rationale: Pi returned 14 findings, all disposition:accept corroborations labelled severity:critical - a combination the review schema's own red-flag list calls incoherent - and its finding 10 credits this change with the prerequisite PR's CONTRACT_VERSION bump. Antigravity returned invalid JSON, which is the unfiled dispatcher fragility already noted in the round-7 resume note.

next_steps: B1: align the packages/gen-eval/Makefile `test` target with the CI selector (-m 'not e2e and not integration'), or repoint tests/test_integration_scenarios.py:45 and tests/test_integration_orchestrator.py:34 at fixtures that exist / skip with a clear message when absent

B2: amend the Descriptor Reclamation requirement and its scenario in openspec/changes/derive-descriptors-from-contracts/specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md:213-227 to require the downstream notice and package-level export correction WITHOUT a JSON Schema contract-version bump; correct the matching claim in packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/descriptor.py:413

H1: for cli-mode-template-only-is-accepted, cli-report-format-json-writes-only-json and cli-no-services-skips-startup - either add a negative-assertion primitive to ExpectBlock (error_excludes, or a file-absence side-effect step) and write discriminating assertions, or move those three units into coverage-exclusions.yaml with the honest reason
M1: warn or fail closed in descriptor.py:377 when `contract:` is set but does not resolve to a readable file (a bogus path currently loads with zero warnings)

M2: dispatch archetypes on the declared kind rather than payload markers in load_descriptor (descriptor.py:389-397), and raise when a descriptor declares a contract but no recognisable archetype payload - pydantic extra:ignore silently discards contract/commands/operations today
M3: consider giving --fail-threshold the same percent semantics and validator as --min-coverage; make dogfood passes 1.0 (a rate) and 1 (a percent) three lines apart

LOW: fix the stale 5-of-17 counts in check_coverage_completeness.py:10-11; document flag-surface.yaml and coverage-exclusions.yaml in evaluation/README.md; catch yaml.parser.ParserError in check_coverage_completeness.main(); document or fix dropped $ref sibling keys in resolve_path_item; intersect the completeness checker's exercised set with the declared set instead of trusting per_interface keys
Rebase before merge - the branch is 23 commits behind main, so green CI here is not green CI on the merge result
